evals.prompt: Validate why this Neovim checkout still opens the live config instead of the worktree when I launch nvim.
evals.expected_behavior: Before trusting any repro or smoke test, the agent confirms the real config root and points `nvim` at the target checkout via `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (set to the parent `.config` directory, not the repo root) and `NVIM_APPNAME`, rather than relying on `cd` alone.
assertions: Identifies the real config root and plugin manager before proposing a fix.
Sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (to the parent `.config` dir) and `NVIM_APPNAME` to target the intended checkout rather than relying on `cd` alone.
Does not trust a repro result until it confirms which checkout `nvim` actually loaded.
deterministic_checks: sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME and NVIM_APPNAME before launching nvim to reproduce

evals.prompt: Add a new keymap and a treesitter textobject config to my Neovim setup, and make sure it doesn't break anything.
evals.expected_behavior: The agent keeps the smallest truthful implementation and validation scope: it implements the keymap/textobject change where the plugin lives, validates with the smallest mode that proves the behavior, and stops probing once the wiring is confirmed instead of re-running every repo-wide validator or restructuring unrelated config.
assertions: Scopes the change to the requested keymap/treesitter config without opportunistically restructuring unrelated plugin wiring.
Chooses the smallest validation mode that proves the change (targeted check) rather than an exhaustive re-validation of the whole config.
Excludes nested `.worktrees/**` when running repo-wide `stylua`/`selene` checks so duplicate checkouts don't produce false failures.

evals.prompt: Fix this Neovim worktree so vim.pack loads blink.cmp v1 and Copilot completions work again.
evals.expected_behavior: The fix pins blink.cmp to `branch = "v1"` (or `version = vim.version.range("^1")`) using a real upstream ref, reacquires the current Copilot client rather than caching it, and the validation proves the plugin's `config` callback side effect actually ran and Copilot completions work — not just that the package is installed.
assertions: Pins blink.cmp to `branch = "v1"` or an equivalent `^1` version range with a real upstream ref, not a lazy.nvim shorthand.
Reacquires the current attached Copilot client per request instead of caching a stale client reference.
Validation confirms the `config` callback's side effect and working completions, not merely that the package appears installed.

evals.prompt: Find the root cause of this failing Lua service test — it's part of our backend, unrelated to any Neovim setup.
evals.expected_behavior: Because the failure is not specific to a Neovim Lua configuration, the agent does not apply neovim-config's checkout/XDG/plugin-wiring workflow and instead uses generic root-cause debugging (`systematic-debugging`).
assertions: Does not apply XDG_CONFIG_HOME/NVIM_APPNAME checkout-targeting steps to a non-Neovim Lua test failure.
Routes toward `systematic-debugging` for the generic root-cause investigation instead.
Does not treat this as a plugin-manager or startup-wiring problem.

evals.prompt: Scaffold a new Neovim plugin called glimpse.nvim that previews file contents in a floating window, with plenary tests and CI.
evals.expected_behavior: Building a new Neovim plugin (structure, plenary tests, CI, doc/ generation) is `neovim-plugin-development`'s surface, not user-level config editing, so the agent routes there instead of treating this as init.lua/lazy.nvim wiring work.
assertions: Does not treat plugin scaffolding (lua/<plugin>/init.lua, tests/, CI) as a user-level config change.
Routes toward `neovim-plugin-development` for building and testing the new plugin.
Does not apply the XDG/checkout-targeting validation steps meant for editing an existing user config.
